# Load data

## Directories

```{r}
# define path to general data main directory
data_dir_main <- here::here("data")

# define path to input directory
input_dir <- here::here( "1_revisions", "2_feature_selection_arcsinh_transformation_median_files")

# define output folder for saving the environment etc. 
output_env_dir <- here::here("1_revisions", "3_Clustering_AL1_cell_median") 
dir.create(output_env_dir)

```

## Data

We will load the csv file containing all cells and the csv file containing the filtered cells that do express at least one feature.

```{r}
# containing the filtered cells
df <- read_csv(paste0(input_dir, 
                              "/cells_median_d3_selected_arcsinh.csv"), 
                   col_types = cols(...1 = col_skip()))

dim(df)
```

# Create seurat object

```{r}
# change meta data information into factors
df$Sample <- factor(df$Sample, levels = unique(df$Sample))

df$Experiment_ID <- factor(df$Experiment_ID, levels = unique(df$Experiment_ID))

df$Condition <- factor(df$Condition, levels = c(
  "CTRL",  "D3"))

CellIDs <- df$CellID

# 2 TRANSPOSE DF -----
df_markers <- df[1:(which(colnames(df) == "Loc_X"))-1] 
df_markers <- sapply(df_markers, as.numeric)
df_t <- t(df_markers)
colnames(df_t) <- CellIDs 
df_meta <- as.data.frame(df[(which(colnames(df) == "Loc_X")):(ncol(df))]) 
rownames(df_meta) <- CellIDs 

# define meta data format
df_meta$CellID <- as.numeric(df_meta$CellID)
df_meta$Loc_X <- as.numeric(df_meta$Loc_X)
df_meta$Loc_Y <- as.numeric(df_meta$Loc_Y)
df_meta$max_features <- NULL

# create seurat object
SO <- CreateSeuratObject(df_t,
                         assay = "MELC", 
                         meta.data = df_meta, 
                         min.features = 2)

features <- colnames(df_markers)
num_features <- length(features)
dim(SO)

# define major features
major_features <- c(
  "CD31", "EMCN", "CD105", "CD200", "CD146", "SMA", 
  "PDPN", "FN", "VIM", "LYVE1", "CD90", "Sca1", "PDGFRa",
  "B220", "CD19", "Kappa", "EpCAM", "CD138",
  "CD45", "CD3", "CD8a", "CD4", "TCRab", 
  "CD68", "CD11b", "CD11c", "Gr1", "CD163", 
  "CD169", "Mac2", "CD44", "MHCII", "Ly6G", "SiglecF", 
  "ST2", "KLRG1", "ICOS", "GATA3eGFP", 
  "TBET", "EOMES", "GZMA", "PRF1"
)
```

Create spatial experiment object

```{r}
set.seed(8)

counts = GetAssayData(SO, layer = "counts")

metadata = SO@meta.data

spatial_coords <- as.matrix(metadata[, c("Loc_X", "Loc_Y")])

spe <- SpatialExperiment(
  assays = list(counts = counts),
  colData = metadata,
  spatialCoords = spatial_coords
)

# Validate the SpatialExperiment object
print(spe)

```

## Exclude marker for cell type clustering

Set markers in the use_channel column to FALSE so they are not used for pca, umap or clustering. Those are markers that are functional and not cell type specific.

I also revised the images and decided to exclude TCRgd, EOMES, and KappaLambda as the images are not optimally adapted or/and have a lot of noise.

```{r}
set.seed(8)

# 1. Define the list of markers to exclude
exclude_markers <- c("Ki67", 
                     "FN", 
                     "CD138"
                     )

# 2. Create the logical mask (TRUE for markers NOT in the exclude list)
rowData(spe)$use_channel <- !(rownames(spe) %in% exclude_markers)

# 3. Verify the result
table(rowData(spe)$use_channel) 
rownames(spe)[!rowData(spe)$use_channel] # Should print excluded markers



```

# Parameter testing

Loop through parameters:

```{r eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}
library(scater)
library(scran)
library(igraph)
library(patchwork)
library(ggplot2)

# --- 1. CONFIGURATION ---

# Define the exact output directory
output_dir <- "D:/Repositories/2025_Kroh_et_al/Murine_ILC_niches_lung_SI_IL-33/1_revisions/3_Clustering_AL1_cell_median/dimensionality_reduction_parameters"
if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE)

# Define your parameter grid (Adjust these ranges as needed)
param_ncomponents <- c(8, 9, 10)       # Number of PCs to calculate
param_nneighbors  <- c(20, 50)         # UMAP n_neighbors (local vs global structure)
param_k           <- c(10, 50, 100, 200, 300, 400)      # KNN k (granularity of Louvain clusters)

# Define the features to plot alongside the clusters
features_to_plot <- c("CD45", "CD31", "PDGFRa", "EpCAM", "CD3", "CD11c", "CD19", "GATA3eGFP")

# --- 2. THE PARAMETER SWEEP LOOP ---

for (nc in param_ncomponents) {
  
  # Step A: Run PCA (Only needs to happen once per 'ncomponents' change)
  message("Running PCA with ", nc, " components...")
  spe <- runPCA(spe, 
                subset_row = rowData(spe)$use_channel, # Exclude DAPI/Ki67 etc.
                exprs_values = "counts", 
                ncomponents = nc,
                BSPARAM = BiocSingular::ExactParam())
  
  for (nn in param_nneighbors) {
    
    # Step B: Run UMAP based on the current PCA
    message("  -> Running UMAP with ", nn, " neighbors...")
    spe <- runUMAP(spe, 
                   dimred = "PCA",       # Crucial: Build UMAP from the PCs, not raw data
                   n_neighbors = nn)
    
    for (k_val in param_k) {
      
      # Step C: Build Graph and Cluster
      message("    --> Clustering with k = ", k_val)
      knn_graph <- buildKNNGraph(spe, use.dimred = "PCA", k = k_val)
      louvain_clusters <- cluster_louvain(knn_graph)
      
      # Store temporary clusters in colData
      colData(spe)$temp_clusters <- as.factor(louvain_clusters$membership)
      
      # Step D: Generate Plots
      # 1. Cluster Plot
      p_cluster <- plotReducedDim(spe, dimred = "UMAP", colour_by = "temp_clusters") +
        ggtitle(paste0("Louvain Clusters (k=", k_val, ")")) +
        theme_classic() +
        theme(legend.position = "right")
      
      # 2. Feature Plots (Loop through features and store in a list)
      feature_plot_list <- list()
      for (feat in features_to_plot) {
        # Check if feature exists to prevent crashes
        if (feat %in% rownames(spe)) {
          # FIXED HERE: Added by_exprs_values = "counts"
          p_feat <- plotReducedDim(spe, dimred = "UMAP", colour_by = feat, by_exprs_values = "counts") +
            ggtitle(feat) +
            theme_classic() +
            theme(legend.position = "right")
          
          feature_plot_list[[feat]] <- p_feat
        } else {
          message("      ⚠️ Feature ", feat, " not found in spe object. Skipping.")
        }
      }
      
      # Step E: Combine all plots using Patchwork
      # Layout: We put the cluster plot first, followed by all the feature plots
      all_plots <- c(list(p_cluster), feature_plot_list)
      
      # Create a master title for the whole image
      plot_title <- paste0("PCA: ", nc, " PCs | UMAP n_neighbors: ", nn, " | KNN k: ", k_val)
      
      # Wrap plots into a 3-column grid
      combined_grid <- wrap_plots(all_plots, ncol = 3) +
        plot_annotation(title = plot_title,
                        theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5)))
      
      # Step F: Construct Filename and Save
      file_name <- paste0("UMAP_PCs-", nc, "_nn-", nn, "_k-", k_val, ".png")
      file_path <- file.path(output_dir, file_name)
      
      # Save the plot (Height/Width adjusted to fit a 3x3 grid comfortably)
      ggsave(filename = file_path, 
             plot = combined_grid, 
             width = 16, 
             height = 12, 
             dpi = 150,       
             bg = "white") 
      
    }
  }
}

message("🎉 Parameter sweep complete! Check your output folder.")
```

# Dimensionality reduction

```{r, fig.height=4, fig.width=6}

set.seed(8)

# define chosen parameters
# Define your parameter grid (Adjust these ranges as needed)
param_ncomponents <- 8      # Number of PCs to calculate
param_nneighbors  <- 50     # UMAP n_neighbors (local vs global structure)
param_k           <- 50     # KNN k (granularity of Louvain clusters)

spe <- runPCA(spe, 
              subset_row = rowData(spe)$use_channel, # Exclude DAPI/Ki67 etc.
              exprs_values = "counts", 
              ncomponents = nc,
              BSPARAM = BiocSingular::ExactParam())


spe <- runUMAP(spe,
               dimred = "PCA", # Crucial: Build UMAP from the PCs, not raw data
               n_neighbors = nn)

# Optional: Plot the variance to confirm 8 PCs is a good cutoff
percent_var <- attr(reducedDim(spe, "PCA"), "percentVar")
if(!is.null(percent_var)) {
  plot(percent_var,
       main = "Scree Plot: Single Sample PCA",
       xlab = "Principal Component",
       ylab = "Variance Explained (%)",
       type = "b",
       pch = 19,
       col = "blue")
  abline(v = 8, col="red", lty=2) 
} else {
  print("Variance attribute not found. Ensure runPCA completed successfully.")
}

# 3. Check the PCA embeddings
pca_embeddings <- reducedDim(spe, "PCA")

print(dim(pca_embeddings))  # Should be [3297 x 8]
print(pca_embeddings[1:5, 1:5])
print(is.numeric(pca_embeddings))          # Should be TRUE
print(any(is.na(pca_embeddings)))          # Should be FALSE
print(any(is.infinite(pca_embeddings)))    # Should be FALSE

# 4. Build the KNN graph directly from the SPE object
# By specifying use.dimred = "PCA", scran handles all matrix orientation automatically
knn_graph <- buildKNNGraph(spe, use.dimred = "PCA", k = k_val)

# Check the number of vertices in the graph
print(igraph::vcount(knn_graph))  # Should be 3297

# 5. Perform Louvain clustering
louvain_clusters <- igraph::cluster_louvain(knn_graph)

# Check the length of the cluster membership vector
print(length(louvain_clusters$membership))  # Should be 3297

# 6. Add cluster labels to the colData of the SpatialExperiment object
colData(spe)$louvain_clusters <- as.factor(louvain_clusters$membership)

# Verify the addition and see the distribution of cells across clusters
print(head(colData(spe)$louvain_clusters))
table(colData(spe)$louvain_clusters)

for (feat in major_features) {
  # Check if feature exists to prevent crashes
  if (feat %in% rownames(spe)) {
    # FIXED HERE: Added by_exprs_values = "counts"
    feat_plot <- plotReducedDim(spe, dimred = "UMAP", colour_by = feat, 
                   by_exprs_values = "counts") +
      ggtitle(feat) +
      theme_classic() +
      theme(legend.position = "right")
    print(feat_plot)
    } else {
      message("      ⚠️ Feature ", feat, " not found in spe object. Skipping.")
    }
}

```

Inspect quality metrics: check if there are low quality clusters with low numbers of features.

```{r, fig.width=9, fig.height=5}
# --- 1. Data Extraction and Preparation ---
plot_data <- as.data.frame(colData(spe)) %>%
  select(
    Clusters = louvain_clusters,
    nCounts = nCount_MELC,      # Total Integrated Intensity per cell
    Detected_Features = nFeature_MELC # Number of markers above background
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Detected_Features, nCounts),
    names_to = "Metric",
    values_to = "Value"
  )

# --- 2. Generate the Linear Violin Plot ---
ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = Clusters, y = Value, fill = Clusters)) +
  # Separate panels for total intensity and feature count
  facet_wrap(~ Metric, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) + 
  
  geom_violin(scale = "width", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.15, outlier.shape = NA, fill = "white") +
  
  # REMOVED: scale_y_continuous(trans = ...) 
  # Using standard linear scale instead
  labs(
    title = "Proteomics QC Metrics by Cluster",
    subtitle = "nFeature: The number of unique features (markers) detected in that cell.\nnCount: The sum of all signal intensities across all markers for that cell.",
    x = "Cluster ID",
    y = "Absolute Value"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 10),
    legend.position = "none",
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "gray90")
  )
```

```{r, fig.width=15, fig.height=10}
# --- 1. Identify Markers of Interest ---
markers_to_plot <- major_features

# --- 2. Extract Expression Data and Merge with Clusters ---
# We pull from the 'counts' assay (your arcsinh data)
expression_matrix <- t(as.matrix(assay(spe, "counts")[markers_to_plot, ]))

plot_data <- as.data.frame(expression_matrix) %>%
  # Add the cluster information from colData
  mutate(Clusters = spe$louvain_clusters) %>%
  # Pivot to long format for ggplot
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(markers_to_plot),
    names_to = "Marker",
    values_to = "Intensity"
  )

# --- 3. Generate the Violin Plot ---
ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = Clusters, y = Intensity, fill = Clusters)) +
  # Create a panel for each protein marker
  facet_wrap(~ Marker, scales = "free_y", ncol = 10) + 
  
  geom_violin(scale = "width", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.15, outlier.shape = NA, fill = "white") +
  
  labs(
    title = "Lineage Marker Expression by Cluster",
    subtitle = "Values are arcsinh-transformed median fluorescence intensities",
    x = "Cluster ID",
    y = "Expression Intensity"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 10),
    legend.position = "none",
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "antiquewhite")
  )
```

```{r, fig.width=9, fig.height=3.5}
#check which markers are used
cat("Total markers:", nrow(spe), "\n")
cat("Markers used for UMAP/PCA:", sum(rowData(spe)$use_channel), "\n")
cat("Excluded markers:", rownames(spe)[!rowData(spe)$use_channel], "\n")


# --- 1. Identify Marker Features (all features) ---
mgs <- findMarkers(spe,

                   direction = "up", 
                   assay.type = "counts") 

# --- 2. Select Top Markers AND filter out excluded ones ---
top_markers <- lapply(mgs, function(df) rownames(df)[df$Top <= 8])

top_markers_filtered <- top_markers[top_markers %in% rownames(spe)[rowData(spe)$use_channel]]

# --- 3. Aggregate Expression ---
pbs <- aggregateAcrossCells(spe, 
                            ids = spe$louvain_clusters, 
                            subset.row = top_markers_filtered, 
                            use.assay.type = "counts", 
                            statistics = "mean")

# --- 4. Plot the Heatmap ---

mat <- t(assay(pbs, "counts"))

pheatmap(mat = mat, 
         scale = "column", 
         clustering_method = "ward.D2",
         color = colorRampPalette(c("#648FFF", "white", "#FFB000"))(101), 
         breaks = seq(-2, 2, length = 101),
         main = "Lineage Markers by Cluster (Functional Markers Excluded)")
```

## Annotation

### 1. The T Cell Compartment (Clusters 6 & 7)

-   **Key Markers:** `CD3+`, `CD8+`, `GZMA+`, `CD45RO+`, `CD103+`, `PD1+`

-   **Annotation:** **Tissue-Resident Memory CD8+ T cells (Trm cells)** and **Cytotoxic T cells**.

-   **Reasoning:** CD3 and CD8 define them as cytotoxic T cells. Granzyme A (GZMA) indicates they are armed for cytotoxicity. CD45RO and CD103 are classic markers for T cells that have taken up permanent residence in mucosal tissues (Trm cells). The high PD1 suggests they are either activated or exhausted from chronic inflammation (typical in periodontitis).

### 2. The B Cell / Plasma Cell Compartment (Clusters 11, 12, & 13)

-   **Key Markers:** `CD45RA+`, `CD27+`, `CD38+` (Notably lacking CD3)

-   **Annotation:** **B cells and Plasma Cells**.

-   **Reasoning:** In the inflamed gingiva, B cells and plasma cells are abundant. CD27 is a classic memory B cell marker, and CD38 is universally highly expressed on plasma cells (which are actively secreting antibodies into the gingival pocket).

### 3. The Endothelial / Vascular Compartment (Clusters 2, 5, & 10)

-   **Key Markers:** `CD31+`, `CD34+`, `COL4+`, `CD49a+`, `SMA+`

-   **Annotation:** **Blood Vessels (Endothelial cells & Pericytes/Smooth Muscle)**.

-   **Reasoning:** CD31 and CD34 are textbook endothelial markers. Collagen IV (COL4) forms the basement membrane of these vessels. Smooth Muscle Actin (SMA) highlights the pericytes or smooth muscle cells wrapping around the larger vessels.

-   *Sub-annotation:* Cluster 5 is strongly CD31+, indicating pure endothelium, while Clusters 2/10 have higher SMA/COL4, suggesting perivascular stroma.

### 4. The Stromal / Fibroblast Compartment (Clusters 3, 8, & 9)

-   **Key Markers:** `PDPN+`, `COL1+`, `CD56+`, `SMA+` (varies)

-   **Annotation:** **Gingival Fibroblasts and Specialized Stroma**.

-   **Reasoning:** Collagen I (COL1) and Podoplanin (PDPN) strongly identify the fibroblastic connective tissue of the gingiva.

-   *Note on your earlier question:* **Cluster 8** is the exact cluster you noticed earlier (PDPN+ CD56+). Seeing it cluster alongside COL1 confirms that this is primarily a stromal/fibroblast population (or an immune-stromal niche) rather than an isolated lymphoid cell.

### 5. The Antigen Presenting Cells (Cluster 1)

-   **Key Markers:** `CD1a+`, `Langerin+`, `CXCR3+`

-   **Annotation:** **Langerhans Cells**.

-   **Reasoning:** As discussed previously, CD1a and Langerin are the definitive, gold-standard markers for Langerhans cells in the mucosal epithelium.

### 6. The Complex Migratory / Macrophage Niche (Cluster 4)

-   **Key Markers:** `CD68+`, `CCR7+`, `CXCR3+`, `CD127+`, `FN+` (Fibronectin), `CAD1+` (E-cadherin)

-   **Annotation:** **Migratory Macrophages / Interacting Niche**.

-   **Reasoning:** CD68 is a classic macrophage marker, and CCR7 indicates these cells are licensed to migrate to lymph nodes. However, the strong co-expression of structural markers like Fibronectin (stroma) and E-cadherin (epithelium) strongly suggests this "cluster" represents a **spatial neighborhood** rather than a single cell type. You are likely capturing macrophages physically squeezing through the epithelial/stromal boundaries or migrating out of the tissue.

```{r, fig.width=9, fig.height=3.5}
# --- 1. Define Canonical Markers for Broad Lineages ---
# Adjust this list to match your exact panel names
main_markers <- c(
# Immune Group
  "CD45", "CD3", "CD27", "CD38", "CD8", "GZMA", "HLA",
  # Vessel Group
  "CD31", "PDPN", "CD34", "VCAM1",
  # Mesenchymal Group
  "SMA", "FN", "COL1", "COL4", 
  "CD1a", "Langerin", "CXCR3", "CAD1", "CD127"
)
# Filter to ensure markers exist in the object
main_markers <- main_markers[main_markers %in% rownames(spe)]

# --- 2. Generate Dot Plot ---
# Shows % of cells expressing (Size) and Mean Intensity (Color)
library(scater)
library(ggplot2)

dot_plot <- plotDots(spe, 
                     features = c(
# Immune Group
  "CD45", "CD1a", "Langerin",
  # Vessel Group
  "CD31", "PDPN", "CD34", "VCAM1",
  # Mesenchymal Group
  "SMA", "FN", "COL1", "COL4"
), 
                     group = "celltypes", 
                     exprs_values = "counts") + 
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 10)) +
  labs(title = "Marker Expression by Annotated Cell Type",
       subtitle = "Dot Size: % of cells expressing; Color: Median intensity (Arcsinh)")+
  coord_flip() # Swaps x and y

print(dot_plot)

# --- 3. Generate Aggregated Heatmap ---
# Step A: Pseudo-bulk aggregation by cell type
library(scuttle) # required for aggregateAcrossCells
pbs_annotated <- aggregateAcrossCells(spe, 
                                      ids = spe$celltypes, 
                                      subset.row = main_markers, 
                                      use.assay.type = "counts", 
                                      statistics = "mean")

# Step B: Extract matrix and Z-score (scale) the data
library(pheatmap)
# Transpose so rows = Cell Types, columns = Markers
mat_annotated <- t(assay(pbs_annotated, "counts"))

# Step C: Plot Heatmap
pheatmap(mat = mat_annotated, 
         scale = "column", 
         clustering_method = "ward.D2",
         color = colorRampPalette(c("#648FFF", "white", "#FFB000"))(101), 
         display_numbers = TRUE, # Optional: shows Z-score values in the cells
         main = "Aggregated Lineage Signatures (Z-scored)")
```

Depict cell types in XY

```{r, fig.width=6, fig.height=5}


# 2. Extract data from the SPE object
# Combining coordinates and metadata
plot_df <- as.data.frame(cbind(spatialCoords(spe), colData(spe)))

# 3. Get the unique samples (FOVs)
# Using 'Filename' as specified in your colData
melced_samples <- unique(plot_df$Filename)

for (sample in melced_samples) {
  
  # Filter for the current FOV
  samp_data <- plot_df %>% filter(Filename == sample)
  n_cells <- nrow(samp_data)
  
  # Create the Spatial Plot
  spatial_plot <- ggplot(samp_data, aes(x = Loc_X, y = Loc_Y, color = celltypes_refined)) + 
    # geom_point to show cells, colored by your specific annotated celltypes
    geom_point(size = 1.5, shape = 20) +
    
    # Custom color palette mapping
    scale_color_manual(values = cols_refined) +
    
    # Standard MELC visualization: black background
    theme_void() +
    theme(
      legend.position = "right",
      legend.text = element_text(color = "white"),
      legend.title = element_text(color = "white", face = "bold"),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = 'black', color = 'black'),
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = 'black', color = 'black'),
      plot.margin = margin(0.2, 0.2, 0.2, 0.2, "cm"),
      plot.title = element_text(size = 14, hjust = 0.5, color = "white")
    ) +
    
    # Reverse Y-axis (microscopy standard)
    scale_y_reverse() +
    
    ggtitle(paste("Sample:", sample, "\nTotal Cells:", n_cells))
  
  # Print the plot
  print(spatial_plot)
}
```

# Export annotated cell types for plotting

## TIFFs celltypes

```{r eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}
library(tiff)

# 1. Setup Output Directory
output_dir_images <- file.path(output_env_dir, "annotated_celltypes_16bit")
if (!dir.exists(output_dir_images)) {
  dir.create(output_dir_images, recursive = TRUE)
}

# 2. Define Dot Radius (Size)
# radius = 1 creates a 3x3 square; radius = 2 creates a 5x5 square
dot_radius <- 2 

# 3. Prepare the data
plot_df <- as.data.frame(cbind(spatialCoords(spe), colData(spe)))
melced_samples <- unique(plot_df$Filename)
all_celltypes  <- unique(plot_df$celltypes)

for (sample in melced_samples) {
  samp_data <- plot_df %>% filter(Filename == sample)
  current_location <- unique(samp_data$Location)
  
  for (ctype in all_celltypes) {
    ctype_data <- samp_data %>% filter(celltypes == ctype)
    if (nrow(ctype_data) == 0) next
    
    # Create an empty 2048x2048 matrix
    mask_matrix <- matrix(0, nrow = 2048, ncol = 2048)
    
    # Round coordinates
    coords <- ctype_data %>%
      mutate(ix = round(Loc_X), iy = round(Loc_Y)) %>%
      filter(ix >= 1 & ix <= 2048 & iy >= 1 & iy <= 2048)
    
    # 4. Draw larger dots
    for(i in seq_len(nrow(coords))) {
      cx <- coords$ix[i]
      cy <- coords$iy[i]
      
      # Define the boundaries for the larger dot, ensuring we stay within image limits
      x_range <- max(1, cx - dot_radius):min(2048, cx + dot_radius)
      y_range <- max(1, cy - dot_radius):min(2048, cy + dot_radius)
      
      # Set the neighborhood to max 16-bit value
      mask_matrix[y_range, x_range] <- 65535
    }
    
    # 5. Define File Path and Write
    file_name <- paste0(sample, "_", current_location, "_", ctype, "_16bit.tif")
    output_path <- file.path(output_dir_images, file_name)
    
    writeTIFF(mask_matrix / 65535, 
              where = output_path, 
              bits.per.sample = 16, 
              reduce = TRUE)
  }
}

message("16-bit Export (Large Dots) complete in: ", output_dir_images)
```

## TIFFs celltypes_refined

```{r eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}

library(tiff)
library(dplyr)

# 1. Setup Output Directory
output_dir_images <- file.path(output_env_dir, "annotated_celltypes_refined_16bit")
if (!dir.exists(output_dir_images)) {
  dir.create(output_dir_images, recursive = TRUE)
}

# 2. Define Dot Radius (Size)
dot_radius <- 2 

# 3. Prepare the data
plot_df <- as.data.frame(cbind(spatialCoords(spe), colData(spe)))
melced_samples <- unique(plot_df$Filename)

# Use the correct refined column for the list
all_celltypes  <- unique(plot_df$celltypes_refined)

for (sample in melced_samples) {
  samp_data <- plot_df %>% filter(Filename == sample)
  current_location <- unique(samp_data$Location)
  
  for (ctype in all_celltypes) {
    # FIXED: Use 'celltypes_refined' here to match the loop variable 'ctype'
    ctype_data <- samp_data %>% filter(celltypes_refined == ctype)
    
    # Skip if this specific cell type is not present in this FOV
    if (nrow(ctype_data) == 0) next
    
    # Create an empty 2048x2048 matrix
    mask_matrix <- matrix(0, nrow = 2048, ncol = 2048)
    
    # Round coordinates
    coords <- ctype_data %>%
      mutate(ix = round(Loc_X), iy = round(Loc_Y)) %>%
      filter(ix >= 1 & ix <= 2048 & iy >= 1 & iy <= 2048)
    
    # 4. Draw dots
    for(i in seq_len(nrow(coords))) {
      cx <- coords$ix[i]
      cy <- coords$iy[i]
      
      # Define boundaries
      x_range <- max(1, cx - dot_radius):min(2048, cx + dot_radius)
      y_range <- max(1, cy - dot_radius):min(2048, cy + dot_radius)
      
      mask_matrix[y_range, x_range] <- 65535
    }
    
    # 5. Define File Path and Write
    # Sanitize ctype name (replaces spaces/slashes with underscores for safe filenames)
    ctype_safe <- gsub("[ /]", "_", ctype)
    file_name <- paste0(sample, "_", current_location, "_", ctype_safe, "_16bit.tif")
    output_path <- file.path(output_dir_images, file_name)
    
    writeTIFF(mask_matrix / 65535, 
              where = output_path, 
              bits.per.sample = 16, 
              reduce = TRUE)
  }
}

message("16-bit Export complete for all refined cell types in: ", output_dir_images)
```

## 7 color TIFF overlay export

All 7 colors (red, green, blue, white, cyan, magenta, and yellow) can be used for channels. In the TIFFs, only 3 channels are interactively usable (red, green, blue), the others are depicted as mixes (Magenta \_ blue + red; Yellow = red + green; Cyan = green + blue).

```{r eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}

# --- 1. CONFIGURATION ---
target_celltype <- "Immune" 

# Set markers for colors. White (chan_w) will now be your cell type.
chan_w <- target_celltype  # WHITE (Cell type of interest)
# if you wanna exclude a channel, set channel to NULL
chan_r <- "FcER1a"             # Red
chan_g <- "CD3"           # Green
chan_b <- "DAPI"           # Blue
chan_m <- "CD27"           # Magenta
chan_y <- "CD56"            # Yellow
chan_c <- "CD38"             # Cyan

# --- 2. DYNAMIC FILENAME & FOLDER SETUP ---
channels <- list(r=chan_r, g=chan_g, b=chan_b, w=chan_w, m=chan_m, y=chan_y, c=chan_c)
active_chans <- channels[!sapply(channels, is.null)]

# Create organized subfolder based on used markers
subfolder_name <- paste(unname(unlist(active_chans)), collapse = "_")
output_dir     <- file.path(output_env_dir, "celltype_overlays", subfolder_name)
if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE)

# --- 3. DATA PREP ---
plot_df <- as.data.frame(cbind(spatialCoords(spe), colData(spe)))
plot_df$Filename <- as.character(plot_df$Filename)
melced_samples <- unique(plot_df$Filename)
dot_radius <- 2 

# Helper: Ensures output is strictly a 2D matrix
load_and_norm <- function(path) {
  if(!file.exists(path)) return(NULL)
  img_raw <- image_read(path) %>% image_data(channels = "gray")
  img_mat <- as.integer(img_raw)[,,1] 
  
  scale <- if(max(img_mat) > 255) 65535 else 255
  return(img_mat / scale)
}

# --- 4. THE PROCESSING LOOP ---
for (current_id in melced_samples) {
  sample_folder <- file.path(raw_image_base, current_id)
  
  # Initialize R, G, B matrices (2D)
  R <- G <- B <- matrix(0, nrow = 2048, ncol = 2048)
  
  for (color in names(active_chans)) {
    marker <- active_chans[[color]]
    
    # Generate Mask if it's the target cell type
    if (marker == target_celltype) {
      val <- matrix(0, nrow = 2048, ncol = 2048)
      coords <- plot_df %>% 
        filter(Filename == current_id & celltypes == target_celltype) %>%
        mutate(ix = round(Loc_X), iy = round(Loc_Y)) %>%
        filter(ix >= (1+dot_radius) & ix <= (2048-dot_radius) & 
               iy >= (1+dot_radius) & iy <= (2048-dot_radius))
      
      if (nrow(coords) > 0) {
        for(i in 1:nrow(coords)) {
          val[(coords$iy[i]-dot_radius):(coords$iy[i]+dot_radius), 
              (coords$ix[i]-dot_radius):(coords$ix[i]+dot_radius)] <- 1
        }
      }
    } else {
      # Load protein images
      val <- load_and_norm(file.path(sample_folder, paste0(marker, ".png")))
      if(is.null(val)) next
    }
    
    # Additive Mixing Logic
    if (color == "r") { R <- R + val }
    if (color == "g") { G <- G + val }
    if (color == "b") { B <- B + val }
    if (color == "w") { R <- R + val; G <- G + val; B <- B + val } # White
    if (color == "m") { R <- R + val; B <- B + val }               # Magenta
    if (color == "y") { R <- R + val; G <- G + val }               # Yellow
    if (color == "c") { G <- G + val; B <- B + val }               # Cyan
  }

  # Clip to 1.0 (prevents intensities exceeding standard range)
  R[R > 1] <- 1; G[G > 1] <- 1; B[B > 1] <- 1
  
  # Build 3D array for TIFF
  overlay_array <- array(0, dim = c(2048, 2048, 3))
  overlay_array[,,1] <- R; overlay_array[,,2] <- G; overlay_array[,,3] <- B
  
  # Construct filename with -color_ naming (e.g., Vessels-w_COL4-g...)
  chan_names <- paste0(unname(unlist(active_chans)), "-", names(active_chans), collapse = "_")
  file_name <- paste0(current_id, "_", chan_names, ".tif")
  # DAPI is always in the blue channel
  # exclude this from name to ensure length of name can be saved
  file_name <- gsub("DAPI-b_|appa|ambda", "", file_name)
  
  writeTIFF(overlay_array, where = file.path(output_dir, file_name), bits.per.sample = 16)
  message(paste("✅ Exported:", file_name))
  rm(R, G, B, overlay_array); gc()
}
```

```{r eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}
chan_c <- NULL             # Cyan (Green + Blue)

active_chans <- channels[!sapply(channels, is.null)]

# Create organized subfolder based on used markers
subfolder_name <- paste(unname(unlist(active_chans)), collapse = "_")
output_dir     <- file.path(output_env_dir, "celltype_overlays", subfolder_name)
if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE)

# --- 3. DATA PREP ---
plot_df <- as.data.frame(cbind(spatialCoords(spe), colData(spe)))
plot_df$Filename <- as.character(plot_df$Filename)
melced_samples <- unique(plot_df$Filename)
dot_radius <- 2 

# Helper: Ensures output is strictly a 2D matrix
load_and_norm <- function(path) {
  if(!file.exists(path)) return(NULL)
  img_raw <- image_read(path) %>% image_data(channels = "gray")
  img_mat <- as.integer(img_raw)[,,1] 
  
  scale <- if(max(img_mat) > 255) 65535 else 255
  return(img_mat / scale)
}

# --- 4. THE PROCESSING LOOP ---
for (current_id in melced_samples) {
  sample_folder <- file.path(raw_image_base, current_id)
  
  # Initialize R, G, B matrices (2D)
  R <- G <- B <- matrix(0, nrow = 2048, ncol = 2048)
  
  for (color in names(active_chans)) {
    marker <- active_chans[[color]]
    
    # Generate Mask if it's the target cell type
    if (marker == target_celltype) {
      val <- matrix(0, nrow = 2048, ncol = 2048)
      coords <- plot_df %>% 
        filter(Filename == current_id & celltypes == target_celltype) %>%
        mutate(ix = round(Loc_X), iy = round(Loc_Y)) %>%
        filter(ix >= (1+dot_radius) & ix <= (2048-dot_radius) & 
               iy >= (1+dot_radius) & iy <= (2048-dot_radius))
      
      if (nrow(coords) > 0) {
        for(i in 1:nrow(coords)) {
          val[(coords$iy[i]-dot_radius):(coords$iy[i]+dot_radius), 
              (coords$ix[i]-dot_radius):(coords$ix[i]+dot_radius)] <- 1
        }
      }
    } else {
      # Load protein images
      val <- load_and_norm(file.path(sample_folder, paste0(marker, ".png")))
      if(is.null(val)) next
    }
    
    # Additive Mixing Logic
    if (color == "r") { R <- R + val }
    if (color == "g") { G <- G + val }
    if (color == "b") { B <- B + val }
    if (color == "w") { R <- R + val; G <- G + val; B <- B + val }
    if (color == "m") { R <- R + val; B <- B + val }
    if (color == "y") { R <- R + val; G <- G + val }
    if (color == "c") { G <- G + val; B <- B + val }
  }

  # Clip to 1.0 (prevents intensities exceeding standard range)
  R[R > 1] <- 1; G[G > 1] <- 1; B[B > 1] <- 1
  
  # Build 3D array for TIFF
  overlay_array <- array(0, dim = c(2048, 2048, 3))
  overlay_array[,,1] <- R; overlay_array[,,2] <- G; overlay_array[,,3] <- B
  
  # Construct filename
  chan_names <- paste0(unname(unlist(active_chans)), "-", names(active_chans), collapse = "_")
  file_name <- paste0(current_id, "_", chan_names, ".tif")
  
  writeTIFF(overlay_array, where = file.path(output_dir, file_name), bits.per.sample = 16)
  message(paste("✅ Exported:", file_name))
  rm(R, G, B, overlay_array); gc()
}

plot_df <- as.data.frame(cbind(spatialCoords(spe), colData(spe)))

dot_radius <- 2 

# Helper: Ensures output is strictly a 2D matrix
load_and_norm <- function(path) {
  if(!file.exists(path)) return(NULL)
  img_raw <- image_read(path) %>% image_data(channels = "gray")
  img_mat <- as.integer(img_raw)[,,1] 
  
  scale <- if(max(img_mat) > 255) 65535 else 255
  return(img_mat / scale)
}

# --- 4. THE PROCESSING LOOP ---
for (current_id in melced_samples) {
  sample_folder <- file.path(raw_image_base, current_id)
  
  # Initialize R, G, B matrices (2D)
  R <- G <- B <- matrix(0, nrow = 2048, ncol = 2048)
  
  for (color in names(active_chans)) {
    marker <- active_chans[[color]]
    
    # Generate Mask if it's the target cell type
    if (marker == target_celltype) {
      val <- matrix(0, nrow = 2048, ncol = 2048)
      coords <- plot_df %>% 
```
```{r eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}
        filter(Filename == current_id & celltypes_refined == target_celltype) %>%
        mutate(ix = round(Loc_X), iy = round(Loc_Y)) %>%
        filter(ix >= (1+dot_radius) & ix <= (2048-dot_radius) & 
               iy >= (1+dot_radius) & iy <= (2048-dot_radius))
      
      if (nrow(coords) > 0) {
        for(i in 1:nrow(coords)) {
          val[(coords$iy[i]-dot_radius):(coords$iy[i]+dot_radius), 
              (coords$ix[i]-dot_radius):(coords$ix[i]+dot_radius)] <- 1
        }
      }
    } else {
      # Load protein images
      val <- load_and_norm(file.path(sample_folder, paste0(marker, ".png")))
      if(is.null(val)) next
    }
    
    # Additive Mixing Logic
    if (color == "r") { R <- R + val }
    if (color == "g") { G <- G + val }
    if (color == "b") { B <- B + val }
    if (color == "w") { R <- R + val; G <- G + val; B <- B + val }
    if (color == "m") { R <- R + val; B <- B + val }
    if (color == "y") { R <- R + val; G <- G + val }
    if (color == "c") { G <- G + val; B <- B + val }
  }

  # Clip to 1.0 (prevents intensities exceeding standard range)
  R[R > 1] <- 1; G[G > 1] <- 1; B[B > 1] <- 1
  
  # Build 3D array for TIFF
  overlay_array <- array(0, dim = c(2048, 2048, 3))
  overlay_array[,,1] <- R; overlay_array[,,2] <- G; overlay_array[,,3] <- B
  
  # Construct filename
  chan_names <- paste0(unname(unlist(active_chans)), "-", names(active_chans), collapse = "_")
  file_name <- paste0(current_id, "_", chan_names, ".tif")
  
  writeTIFF(overlay_array, where = file.path(output_dir, file_name), bits.per.sample = 16)
  message(paste("✅ Exported:", file_name))
  rm(R, G, B, overlay_array); gc()
}

channels <- list(r=chan_r, g=chan_g, b=chan_b, w=chan_w, m=chan_m, y=chan_y, c=chan_c)
active_chans <- channels[!sapply(channels, is.null)]

# Create organized subfolder based on used markers
subfolder_name <- paste(unname(unlist(active_chans)), collapse = "_")
output_dir     <- file.path(output_env_dir, "celltype_overlays", subfolder_name)
if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE)

# --- 3. DATA PREP ---
plot_df <- as.data.frame(cbind(spatialCoords(spe), colData(spe)))
plot_df$Filename <- as.character(plot_df$Filename)
melced_samples <- unique(plot_df$Filename)
dot_radius <- 2 

# Helper: Ensures output is strictly a 2D matrix
load_and_norm <- function(path) {
  if(!file.exists(path)) return(NULL)
  img_raw <- image_read(path) %>% image_data(channels = "gray")
  img_mat <- as.integer(img_raw)[,,1] 
  
  scale <- if(max(img_mat) > 255) 65535 else 255
  return(img_mat / scale)
}

# --- 4. THE PROCESSING LOOP ---
for (current_id in melced_samples) {
  sample_folder <- file.path(raw_image_base, current_id)
  
  # Initialize R, G, B matrices (2D)
  R <- G <- B <- matrix(0, nrow = 2048, ncol = 2048)
  
  for (color in names(active_chans)) {
    marker <- active_chans[[color]]
    
    # Generate Mask if it's the target cell type
    if (marker == target_celltype) {
      val <- matrix(0, nrow = 2048, ncol = 2048)
      coords <- plot_df %>% 
        filter(Filename == current_id & celltypes_refined == target_celltype) %>%
        mutate(ix = round(Loc_X), iy = round(Loc_Y)) %>%
        filter(ix >= (1+dot_radius) & ix <= (2048-dot_radius) & 
               iy >= (1+dot_radius) & iy <= (2048-dot_radius))
      
      if (nrow(coords) > 0) {
        for(i in 1:nrow(coords)) {
          val[(coords$iy[i]-dot_radius):(coords$iy[i]+dot_radius), 
              (coords$ix[i]-dot_radius):(coords$ix[i]+dot_radius)] <- 1
        }
      }
    } else {
      # Load protein images
      val <- load_and_norm(file.path(sample_folder, paste0(marker, ".png")))
      if(is.null(val)) next
    }
    
    # Additive Mixing Logic
    if (color == "r") { R <- R + val }
    if (color == "g") { G <- G + val }
    if (color == "b") { B <- B + val }
    if (color == "w") { R <- R + val; G <- G + val; B <- B + val }
    if (color == "m") { R <- R + val; B <- B + val }
    if (color == "y") { R <- R + val; G <- G + val }
    if (color == "c") { G <- G + val; B <- B + val }
  }

  # Clip to 1.0 (prevents intensities exceeding standard range)
  R[R > 1] <- 1; G[G > 1] <- 1; B[B > 1] <- 1
  
  # Build 3D array for TIFF
  overlay_array <- array(0, dim = c(2048, 2048, 3))
  overlay_array[,,1] <- R; overlay_array[,,2] <- G; overlay_array[,,3] <- B
  
  # Construct filename
  chan_names <- paste0(unname(unlist(active_chans)), "-", names(active_chans), collapse = "_")
  file_name <- paste0(current_id, "_", chan_names, ".tif")
  
  writeTIFF(overlay_array, where = file.path(output_dir, file_name), bits.per.sample = 16)
  message(paste("✅ Exported:", file_name))
  rm(R, G, B, overlay_array); gc()
}

channels <- list(r=chan_r, g=chan_g, b=chan_b, w=chan_w, m=chan_m, y=chan_y, c=chan_c)
active_chans <- channels[!sapply(channels, is.null)]

# Create organized subfolder based on used markers
subfolder_name <- paste(unname(unlist(active_chans)), collapse = "_")
output_dir     <- file.path(output_env_dir, "celltype_overlays", subfolder_name)
if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE)

# --- 3. DATA PREP ---
plot_df <- as.data.frame(cbind(spatialCoords(spe), colData(spe)))
plot_df$Filename <- as.character(plot_df$Filename)
melced_samples <- unique(plot_df$Filename)
dot_radius <- 2 

# Helper: Ensures output is strictly a 2D matrix
load_and_norm <- function(path) {
  if(!file.exists(path)) return(NULL)
  img_raw <- image_read(path) %>% image_data(channels = "gray")
  img_mat <- as.integer(img_raw)[,,1] 
  
  scale <- if(max(img_mat) > 255) 65535 else 255
  return(img_mat / scale)
}

# --- 4. THE PROCESSING LOOP ---
for (current_id in melced_samples) {
  sample_folder <- file.path(raw_image_base, current_id)
  
  # Initialize R, G, B matrices (2D)
  R <- G <- B <- matrix(0, nrow = 2048, ncol = 2048)
  
  for (color in names(active_chans)) {
    marker <- active_chans[[color]]
    
    # Generate Mask if it's the target cell type
    if (marker == target_celltype) {
      val <- matrix(0, nrow = 2048, ncol = 2048)
      coords <- plot_df %>% 
        filter(Filename == current_id & celltypes_refined == target_celltype) %>%
        mutate(ix = round(Loc_X), iy = round(Loc_Y)) %>%
        filter(ix >= (1+dot_radius) & ix <= (2048-dot_radius) & 
               iy >= (1+dot_radius) & iy <= (2048-dot_radius))
      
      if (nrow(coords) > 0) {
        for(i in 1:nrow(coords)) {
          val[(coords$iy[i]-dot_radius):(coords$iy[i]+dot_radius), 
              (coords$ix[i]-dot_radius):(coords$ix[i]+dot_radius)] <- 1
        }
      }
    } else {
      # Load protein images
      val <- load_and_norm(file.path(sample_folder, paste0(marker, ".png")))
      if(is.null(val)) next
    }
    
    # Additive Mixing Logic
    if (color == "r") { R <- R + val }
    if (color == "g") { G <- G + val }
    if (color == "b") { B <- B + val }
    if (color == "w") { R <- R + val; G <- G + val; B <- B + val }
    if (color == "m") { R <- R + val; B <- B + val }
    if (color == "y") { R <- R + val; G <- G + val }
    if (color == "c") { G <- G + val; B <- B + val }
  }

  # Clip to 1.0 (prevents intensities exceeding standard range)
  R[R > 1] <- 1; G[G > 1] <- 1; B[B > 1] <- 1
  
  # Build 3D array for TIFF
  overlay_array <- array(0, dim = c(2048, 2048, 3))
  overlay_array[,,1] <- R; overlay_array[,,2] <- G; overlay_array[,,3] <- B
  
  # Construct filename
  chan_names <- paste0(unname(unlist(active_chans)), "-", names(active_chans), collapse = "_")
  file_name <- paste0(current_id, "_", chan_names, ".tif")
  
  writeTIFF(overlay_array, where = file.path(output_dir, file_name), bits.per.sample = 16)
  message(paste("✅ Exported:", file_name))
  rm(R, G, B, overlay_array); gc()
}

plot_df <- as.data.frame(cbind(spatialCoords(spe), colData(spe)))
plot_df$Filename <- as.character(plot_df$Filename)
melced_samples <- unique(plot_df$Filename)
dot_radius <- 2 

# Helper: Ensures output is strictly a 2D matrix
load_and_norm <- function(path) {
  if(!file.exists(path)) return(NULL)
  img_raw <- image_read(path) %>% image_data(channels = "gray")
  img_mat <- as.integer(img_raw)[,,1] 
  
  scale <- if(max(img_mat) > 255) 65535 else 255
  return(img_mat / scale)
}

# --- 4. THE PROCESSING LOOP ---
for (current_id in melced_samples) {
  sample_folder <- file.path(raw_image_base, current_id)
  
  # Initialize R, G, B matrices (2D)
  R <- G <- B <- matrix(0, nrow = 2048, ncol = 2048)
  
  for (color in names(active_chans)) {
    marker <- active_chans[[color]]
    
    # Generate Mask if it's the target cell type
    if (marker == target_celltype) {
      val <- matrix(0, nrow = 2048, ncol = 2048)
      coords <- plot_df %>% 
        filter(Filename == current_id & celltypes_refined == target_celltype) %>%
        mutate(ix = round(Loc_X), iy = round(Loc_Y)) %>%
        filter(ix >= (1+dot_radius) & ix <= (2048-dot_radius) & 
               iy >= (1+dot_radius) & iy <= (2048-dot_radius))
      
      if (nrow(coords) > 0) {
        for(i in 1:nrow(coords)) {
          val[(coords$iy[i]-dot_radius):(coords$iy[i]+dot_radius), 
              (coords$ix[i]-dot_radius):(coords$ix[i]+dot_radius)] <- 1
        }
      }
    } else {
      # Load protein images
      val <- load_and_norm(file.path(sample_folder, paste0(marker, ".png")))
      if(is.null(val)) next
    }
    
    # Additive Mixing Logic
    if (color == "r") { R <- R + val }
    if (color == "g") { G <- G + val }
    if (color == "b") { B <- B + val }
    if (color == "w") { R <- R + val; G <- G + val; B <- B + val }
    if (color == "m") { R <- R + val; B <- B + val }
    if (color == "y") { R <- R + val; G <- G + val }
    if (color == "c") { G <- G + val; B <- B + val }
  }

  # Clip to 1.0 (prevents intensities exceeding standard range)
  R[R > 1] <- 1; G[G > 1] <- 1; B[B > 1] <- 1
  
  # Build 3D array for TIFF
  overlay_array <- array(0, dim = c(2048, 2048, 3))
  overlay_array[,,1] <- R; overlay_array[,,2] <- G; overlay_array[,,3] <- B
  
  # Construct filename
  chan_names <- paste0(unname(unlist(active_chans)), "-", names(active_chans), collapse = "_")
  file_name <- paste0(current_id, "_", chan_names, ".tif")
  
  writeTIFF(overlay_array, where = file.path(output_dir, file_name), bits.per.sample = 16)
  message(paste("✅ Exported:", file_name))
  rm(R, G, B, overlay_array); gc()
}

# Helper: Ensures output is strictly a 2D matrix
load_and_norm <- function(path) {
  if(!file.exists(path)) return(NULL)
  img_raw <- image_read(path) %>% image_data(channels = "gray")
  img_mat <- as.integer(img_raw)[,,1] 
  
  scale <- if(max(img_mat) > 255) 65535 else 255
  return(img_mat / scale)
}

# --- 4. THE PROCESSING LOOP ---
for (current_id in melced_samples) {
  sample_folder <- file.path(raw_image_base, current_id)
  
  # Initialize R, G, B matrices (2D)
  R <- G <- B <- matrix(0, nrow = 2048, ncol = 2048)
  
  for (color in names(active_chans)) {
    marker <- active_chans[[color]]
    
    # Generate Mask if it's the target cell type
    if (marker == target_celltype) {
      val <- matrix(0, nrow = 2048, ncol = 2048)
      coords <- plot_df %>% 
        filter(Filename == current_id & celltypes_refined == target_celltype) %>%
        mutate(ix = round(Loc_X), iy = round(Loc_Y)) %>%
        filter(ix >= (1+dot_radius) & ix <= (2048-dot_radius) & 
               iy >= (1+dot_radius) & iy <= (2048-dot_radius))
      
      if (nrow(coords) > 0) {
        for(i in 1:nrow(coords)) {
          val[(coords$iy[i]-dot_radius):(coords$iy[i]+dot_radius), 
              (coords$ix[i]-dot_radius):(coords$ix[i]+dot_radius)] <- 1
        }
      }
    } else {
      # Load protein images
      val <- load_and_norm(file.path(sample_folder, paste0(marker, ".png")))
      if(is.null(val)) next
    }
    
    # Additive Mixing Logic
    if (color == "r") { R <- R + val }
    if (color == "g") { G <- G + val }
    if (color == "b") { B <- B + val }
    if (color == "w") { R <- R + val; G <- G + val; B <- B + val }
    if (color == "m") { R <- R + val; B <- B + val }
    if (color == "y") { R <- R + val; G <- G + val }
    if (color == "c") { G <- G + val; B <- B + val }
  }

  # Clip to 1.0 (prevents intensities exceeding standard range)
  R[R > 1] <- 1; G[G > 1] <- 1; B[B > 1] <- 1
  
  # Build 3D array for TIFF
  overlay_array <- array(0, dim = c(2048, 2048, 3))
  overlay_array[,,1] <- R; overlay_array[,,2] <- G; overlay_array[,,3] <- B
  
  # Construct filename
  chan_names <- paste0(unname(unlist(active_chans)), "-", names(active_chans), collapse = "_")
  file_name <- paste0(current_id, "_", chan_names, ".tif")
  
  writeTIFF(overlay_array, where = file.path(output_dir, file_name), bits.per.sample = 16)
  message(paste("✅ Exported:", file_name))
  rm(R, G, B, overlay_array); gc()
}

channels <- list(r=chan_r, g=chan_g, b=chan_b, w=chan_w, m=chan_m, y=chan_y, c=chan_c)
active_chans <- channels[!sapply(channels, is.null)]

# Create organized subfolder based on used markers
subfolder_name <- paste(unname(unlist(active_chans)), collapse = "_")
output_dir     <- file.path(output_env_dir, "celltype_overlays", subfolder_name)
if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE)

# --- 3. DATA PREP ---
plot_df <- as.data.frame(cbind(spatialCoords(spe), colData(spe)))
plot_df$Filename <- as.character(plot_df$Filename)
melced_samples <- unique(plot_df$Filename)
dot_radius <- 2 

# Helper: Ensures output is strictly a 2D matrix
load_and_norm <- function(path) {
  if(!file.exists(path)) return(NULL)
  img_raw <- image_read(path) %>% image_data(channels = "gray")
  img_mat <- as.integer(img_raw)[,,1] 
  
  scale <- if(max(img_mat) > 255) 65535 else 255
  return(img_mat / scale)
}

# --- 4. THE PROCESSING LOOP ---
for (current_id in melced_samples) {
  sample_folder <- file.path(raw_image_base, current_id)
  
  # Initialize R, G, B matrices (2D)
  R <- G <- B <- matrix(0, nrow = 2048, ncol = 2048)
  
  for (color in names(active_chans)) {
    marker <- active_chans[[color]]
    
    # Generate Mask if it's the target cell type
    if (marker == target_celltype) {
      val <- matrix(0, nrow = 2048, ncol = 2048)
      coords <- plot_df %>% 
        filter(Filename == current_id & celltypes_refined == target_celltype) %>%
        mutate(ix = round(Loc_X), iy = round(Loc_Y)) %>%
        filter(ix >= (1+dot_radius) & ix <= (2048-dot_radius) & 
               iy >= (1+dot_radius) & iy <= (2048-dot_radius))
      
      if (nrow(coords) > 0) {
        for(i in 1:nrow(coords)) {
          val[(coords$iy[i]-dot_radius):(coords$iy[i]+dot_radius), 
              (coords$ix[i]-dot_radius):(coords$ix[i]+dot_radius)] <- 1
        }
      }
    } else {
      # Load protein images
      val <- load_and_norm(file.path(sample_folder, paste0(marker, ".png")))
      if(is.null(val)) next
    }
    
    # Additive Mixing Logic
    if (color == "r") { R <- R + val }
    if (color == "g") { G <- G + val }
    if (color == "b") { B <- B + val }
    if (color == "w") { R <- R + val; G <- G + val; B <- B + val }
    if (color == "m") { R <- R + val; B <- B + val }
    if (color == "y") { R <- R + val; G <- G + val }
    if (color == "c") { G <- G + val; B <- B + val }
  }

  # Clip to 1.0 (prevents intensities exceeding standard range)
  R[R > 1] <- 1; G[G > 1] <- 1; B[B > 1] <- 1
  
  # Build 3D array for TIFF
  overlay_array <- array(0, dim = c(2048, 2048, 3))
  overlay_array[,,1] <- R; overlay_array[,,2] <- G; overlay_array[,,3] <- B
  
  # Construct filename
  chan_names <- paste0(unname(unlist(active_chans)), "-", names(active_chans), collapse = "_")
  file_name <- paste0(current_id, "_", chan_names, ".tif")
  
  writeTIFF(overlay_array, where = file.path(output_dir, file_name), bits.per.sample = 16)
  message(paste("✅ Exported:", file_name))
  rm(R, G, B, overlay_array); gc()
}
```

```{r, fig.width=9, fig.height=2.5}
# 1. Create the summary data frame with forced alphabetical sorting
summary_df <- as.data.frame(colData(spe)) %>%
  # Convert to character to drop any existing factor level ordering
```

# Data inspection for follow up analysis

We will visulaize the clusters in a heatmap with all the markers that were used for the analysis:

```{r, fig.width=9, fig.height=5}

# 1. Extract the names of the markers where use_channel is TRUE
selected_markers <- rownames(spe)[rowData(spe)$use_channel]
library(dittoSeq)

# 1. "Nuke" the factor by converting to raw character strings 
# This completely destroys any hidden "ghost" levels
colData(spe)$celltypes_refined <- as.character(colData(spe)$celltypes_refined)

# 2. Re-build the factor cleanly from scratch
colData(spe)$celltypes_refined <- as.factor(colData(spe)$celltypes_refined)

# 3. Get the absolute, true levels that exist right now
true_levels <- levels(colData(spe)$celltypes_refined)
message("Levels actually present in the data: ", paste(true_levels, collapse = ", "))

# 4. Pull ONLY the necessary colors from your cols_refined palette
matching_colors <- cols_refined[true_levels]

# 5. Extract the selected markers
selected_markers <- rownames(spe)[rowData(spe)$use_channel]

# 6. Generate the Heatmap
dittoHeatmap(
    object = spe,
    genes = selected_markers,
    annot.by = "celltypes_refined",
    order.by = "celltypes_refined",
    assay = "counts",
    scaled.to.max = TRUE,             
    cluster_cols = FALSE,             
    show_colnames = FALSE,            
    main = "Expression of Selected Lymphocyte Markers",
    # Pass the perfectly matched subset of your custom colors
    annotation_colors = list(celltypes_refined = matching_colors)
)
```

We could already separate B cells/Plasma cells from T cells. We will now check how decent the separation is in order to evaluate if we recluster them together as lymphocytes or separately.

```{r, fig.width=9, fig.height=3}

# 1. Use the %in% operator to match multiple cell types in colData
# This creates a logical vector (TRUE for your targets, FALSE for others)
lymphocyte_indices <- spe$celltypes_refined %in% c("Tcells", "BcellsPCs")

# 2. Subset the spe object (Rows = Markers, Columns = Cells)
# We keep all rows (markers) and only the selected columns (cells)
spe_lympho <- spe[, lymphocyte_indices]

# 3. Optional: Verify the subset
table(spe_lympho$celltypes_refined)
dim(spe_lympho)

# 1. Extract the names of the markers where use_channel is TRUE

  #"EOMES", 
  "CD45RA", "CD45RO", 
  "CCR7",
  "CD69", "CD38", "PD1", "HLA", 
  "CD103",
  "CD49a",
  "GZMA", #"Ki67", 
  #"CD117", 
  "CD127", "CD27", "CXCR3", "CAD1", "CD31"
)


# 1. "Nuke" the factor by converting to raw character strings 
# This completely destroys any hidden "ghost" levels
colData(spe_lympho)$celltypes_refined <- as.character(colData(spe_lympho)$celltypes_refined)

# 2. Re-build the factor cleanly from scratch
colData(spe_lympho)$celltypes_refined <- as.factor(colData(spe_lympho)$celltypes_refined)

# 3. Get the absolute, true levels that exist right now
true_levels <- levels(colData(spe_lympho)$celltypes_refined)
message("Levels actually present in the data: ", paste(true_levels, collapse = ", "))

# 4. Pull ONLY the necessary colors from your cols_refined palette
matching_colors <- cols_refined[true_levels]

# 6. Generate the Heatmap
dittoHeatmap(
    object = spe_lympho,
    genes = selected_markers,
    annot.by = "celltypes_refined",
    order.by = "celltypes_refined",
    assay = "counts",
    scaled.to.max = TRUE,             
    cluster_cols = FALSE,             
    show_colnames = FALSE,            
    main = "Expression of Selected Lymphocyte Markers",
    # Pass the perfectly matched subset of your custom colors
    annotation_colors = list(celltypes_refined = matching_colors)
)
```

The separation is decent, so we will do the reclustering with T cells and B cells/Plasma cells separately. The T cell cluster might also contain ILCs and NK cells.

## UMAP AL1

```{r, fig.width=5.5, fig.height=4.5}
spe_plot <- spe

# 1. Convert to character
spe_plot$celltypes_refined <- as.character(spe_plot$celltypes_refined)

# 2. Bulk rename using case_match
spe_plot$celltypes_refined <- case_match(
  spe_plot$celltypes_refined,
  "Tcells"      ~ "Immune II",
  "BcellsPCs"      ~ "Immune I",
  "Undefined" ~ "Stroma/Epithelia",
  "Stroma" ~ "Stroma/Epithelia",
  "Langerhans" ~ "Stroma/Epithelia",
  # The .default argument ensures any cell type you DON'T list above 
  # (like Fibroblasts) simply keeps its original name.
  .default = spe_plot$celltypes_refined 
)

# 3. Convert back to a factor
spe_plot$celltypes_refined <- as.factor(spe_plot$celltypes_refined)

cols_al1 <- c(
  "Immune I"      = "#117733",  
  "Immune II" = "#DDCC77",  
  "Vessels"          = "#882255",  
  "Stroma/Epithelia"        = "#332288"
)

plot_umap <- dittoDimPlot(spe_plot, var = "celltypes_refined", 
                   reduction.use = "UMAP_harmony", size = 0.5) +
    ggtitle("AL1 cell types") + 
  scale_color_manual(name = "AL1", values = cols_al1)+
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

plot_umap
```

Heatmap AL1

```{r, fig.width=9, fig.height=3}

# --- 2. Generate Aggregated Heatmap ---

# Step A: Pseudo-bulk aggregation by the three cell types
# Using a broader marker set to define the functional landscape
pbs_annotated <- scuttle::aggregateAcrossCells(spe_plot, 
                                      ids = spe_plot$celltypes_refined, 
                                      subset.row = rownames(spe)[rowData(spe)$use_channel], 
                                      use.assay.type = "counts", 
                                      statistics = "mean")

# Step B: Extract matrix and scale
# We transpose so the 3 cell types are on one axis and markers on the other
mat_annotated <- t(assay(pbs_annotated, "counts"))

# Step C: Plot Heatmap
# ward.D2 clustering will group markers that behave similarly across Tcells/ILCs/Other APCs
plot_heat <- ComplexHeatmap::pheatmap(mat = mat_annotated, 
         scale = "column", 
         clustering_method = "ward.D2",
         color = colorRampPalette(c("#648FFF", "white", "#FFB000"))(101), # Using your palette colors
         display_numbers = FALSE, 
         number_color = "black",
         fontsize_number = 8,
         main = "AL1 - Aggregated Lineage Signatures (Z-scored)",
         name = "Z-Score" # This becomes your legend title!)
)

plot_heat
```

```{r, fig.width=5.5, fig.height=4.5, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(scater)

# --- 1. DEFINE LINEAGE MARKERS ---

lineage_markers <- c(

 )

# NEW: Define the exact desired order for the cell types
cell_order <- c("Immune I", "Immune II", "Stroma/Epithelia", "Vessels")

# Apply the factor levels to the spe object to lock in the order
spe_plot$celltypes_refined <- factor(spe_plot$celltypes_refined, levels = cell_order)
# Ensure we only use markers actually present in the spe object to prevent errors
valid_markers <- intersect(lineage_markers, rownames(spe_plot))

plot_dot <- plotDots(spe_plot, 
         features = valid_markers, 
         group = "celltypes_refined", 
         exprs_values = "counts", # Uses your base assay. Change to "logcounts" if you have transformed data.
         scale = TRUE) +          # Z-scales the colors across cell types for better contrast

    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 12),

  )+
  scale_color_gradientn(colors = cols_heat)
```

```{r, fig.width=12, fig.height=7.4}

# 2. Prepare and combine data
plot_df <- as.data.frame(cbind(spatialCoords(spe_plot), colData(spe_plot))) %>%
  # Create the combined label
  mutate(Facet_Label = paste0(Filename)) %>%
  # REORDER LOGIC: Arrange by Condition then Filename
  arrange(factor(Condition, levels = c("HD", "PD")), Filename) %>%
  # Lock in this order
  mutate(Facet_Label = factor(Facet_Label, levels = unique(Facet_Label)))

# 3. Create the faceted overview plot
grid_plot <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = Loc_X, y = Loc_Y, color = celltypes_refined)) +
  # Using smaller points for the grid to avoid overplotting
  geom_point(size = 0.4, shape = 20, alpha = 0.8) +
  # Faceting
  facet_wrap(~ Facet_Label, ncol = 6) +
  # Use manual colors
  scale_color_manual(values = cols_al1) +
  # INCREASE LEGEND SYMBOL SIZE
  guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 5, alpha = 1))) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "black", color = "grey30", 
                                    linewidth = 0.2),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "black"),
    strip.text = element_text(color = "white", face = "bold", size = 9, 
                              margin = margin(b = 5)),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.text = element_text(color = "white"),
    legend.title = element_text(color = "white", face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(color = "white", hjust = 0.5, size = 16, 
                              margin = margin(t = 10, b = 10))
  ) +
  scale_y_reverse() +
  labs(
    title = "Spatial Distribution AL1",
    color = "AL1"
  ) +
  # Use coord_fixed to ensure tissue geometry is not distorted
  coord_fixed()

# 4. Print the grid
print(grid_plot)
```
